assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted a magic angle with flat moire bands from a clean, analytically transparent mechanism, and the 2018 experiments showed correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable platform. This opened a whole field of moire quantum matter, a rare case of a simple model that organised a messy many-body problem and was confirmed by experiment.
assessment.attribution: Theory credit sits with Bistritzer and MacDonald (2011); experimental discovery with Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators (Cao et al. 2018). A theory-plus-experiment configuration is natural, though Bistritzer as a postdoc and other experimental groups (e.g. Dean, Yazdani, Young) complicate any three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups reproduced the correlated and superconducting phases and the field is still growing; the basic single-particle picture is stable, while the origin of the superconductivity remains open. Timing is good, since the discovery is nearly a decade old.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is not settled
Whether the flat-band theory or the 2018 experiments are weighted more heavily is open
Contributions of earlier theory (e.g. Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) and other experimental groups may be argued

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reaching 1e-18 fractional uncertainty rest on the magic-wavelength idea and Sr/Yb lattice spectroscopy, giving the most accurate measurements ever made and enabling relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants. The idea is simple and general, and its impact on metrology is clear.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock; Ye brought it to the 1e-18 level and many-body clock physics. A two-person award is clean, with Hall and Haensch already recognised for the frequency comb. Other groups (e.g. Lemonde, Bloom, Hinkley) form a wider credit set.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by multiple laboratories worldwide, with ongoing work toward redefinition of the SI second; the technology is mature and recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Boundary with ion-clock work and comb contributions already honoured in 2005
Whether the committee prefers an award tied to a redefinition of the second

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cavity method and survey-propagation message passing turned spin-glass ideas into algorithms and a rigorous-style picture of glassy transitions in random constraint-satisfaction problems. It exemplifies the statistical physics of disordered systems applied to computation and inference, a theme close to the learning/physics link already honoured in 2024.
assessment.attribution: Mezard, Parisi and Virasoro developed the cavity method for spin glasses; the satisfiability applications are credited to Mezard and Zecchina. Parisi was already awarded in 2021, so the remaining credit configuration is narrower and some of the foundational credit is already recognised.
assessment.maturity: Several of the predictions about satisfiability thresholds have been backed by rigorous mathematical results, but the practical impact on algorithms is more mixed. Recognition could be seen as a follow-up to 2021.
uncertainties: Overlap with the Parisi spin-glass prize of 2021 and whether this is a distinct discovery
Experimental or practical confirmation is largely mathematical and computational
Role of other contributors (Monasson, Kirkpatrick, Mezard-Parisi-Virasoro) in attribution

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Inflation explains flatness, horizon uniformity and the origin of primordial fluctuations through a simple dynamical mechanism, and the predicted nearly scale-invariant spectrum matches CMB data. The quantum origin of structure is a striking universal mechanism.
assessment.attribution: Guth, Linde, Albrecht-Steinhardt, Starobinsky and Mukhanov-Chibisov all contributed decisively; the supplied credit omits Starobinsky and Sato, so the fair allocation is contested. Of the supplied names, Guth, Linde and Mukhanov cover idea, new inflation and fluctuations.
assessment.maturity: Observational support from CMB is strong but indirect; no detection of primordial gravitational waves, and alternatives are not definitively excluded. The prize has been waiting a long time and the field has seen a 2006 award on the CMB.
uncertainties: Attribution of credit among Starobinsky, Guth, Linde, Sato, Mukhanov and others
Lack of a decisive observational test (tensor modes)
Model dependence of the inflationary paradigm

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The KTHNY theory describes two-dimensional melting by dislocation and disclination unbinding and predicts the hexatic phase, with universal exponents. It is a clean, analytically tractable mechanism with wide use in soft matter and colloids and confirmed in many systems.
assessment.attribution: Halperin and Nelson (and Young) extended Kosterlitz-Thouless to melting; Kosterlitz and Thouless already received the 2016 prize for the related topological defect theory, so the remaining credit may be seen as derivative.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation in colloids, liquid crystals and electron systems is extensive, though the order of the transition is system dependent. The theory is old, so recognition would be late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether this is sufficiently distinct from the 2016 prize
Young's credit versus others and systems where the transition is first order

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Higgs boson discovery was a milestone confirming the mechanism of mass in the Standard Model, and the ATLAS and CMS detectors were extraordinary experimental achievements. The scientific importance is beyond doubt, though the committee already recognised the theory in 2013.
assessment.attribution: Awarding the conception and construction leaders of ATLAS and CMS is the main route available, but credit is distributed over thousands of collaborators and many other leaders (spokespersons, accelerator builders, Evans) and the Nobel rules limit to three.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed and measured with many decay channels; timing is a long-standing question, since the physics recognition has already been given.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit cannot be allocated cleanly to three people
Whether the discovery was already recognised in 2013
Competing claims (Evans for LHC, physics analysis leaders)

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised Hubbard-type models, the Mott transition and many-body dynamics in a controlled setting, linking condensed-matter theory and experiment in a way that appeals strongly to statistical physicists.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Cirac proposed the schemes; Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger realised them. A three-person configuration forces uneven choices, and Zoller and Cirac also appear in other candidates.
assessment.maturity: Many groups have reproduced results and the field is mature; the open question is whether the quantum-simulation payoff will be considered decisive yet.
uncertainties: Contested split between theory proposals and experiments
Overlap with other quantum-information candidates and the 2012/2022/2025 prizes

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organising principle of cell interiors is a conceptually simple physical mechanism with large biological consequences, and the physical theory of active droplets links soft-matter and non-equilibrium statistical physics to biology.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne made the 2009 P-granule discovery; Julicher supplied the physical theory of active droplets. The configuration is plausible, but the discovery lies at the boundary of physics and biology/chemistry and other contributors (e.g. Rosen, Parker, Pappu) could be credited.
assessment.maturity: The idea is widely adopted but debated: how generally phase separation explains cellular function and its in vivo relevance are still disputed. Recognition might be premature or better suited to another prize.
uncertainties: Whether the discovery is physics or biology for prize purposes
Controversy over in vivo relevance and generality of condensates
Attribution of credit among many contributors
